1.q: וּ⁠בִ⁠שְׁנַת֙ שְׁמֹנֶ֣ה עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לַ⁠מֶּ֖לֶךְ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֑ט מָלַ֥ךְ אֲבִיָּ֖ם עַל־יְהוּדָֽה
1.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is introducing **Abijam** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Judah**. Your language may have its own way of introducing participants that you can use in your translation. See the discussion in the introduction to this chapter of how the author is, for the first time in the book, referring here to a year in the reign of the king of one kingdom in order to identify when the king of another kingdom began to reign.

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **the year of 18**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [Now in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam]

See the discussion in the introduction to chapter 14 of the form of this name. We recommend that you use the name **Abijam** in your translation here and not try to harmonize it with the form “Abijah” that appears in 2 Chronicles.

3.note: See how you translated the similar expression “to walk in his ways” in 2:3. Alternate translation: [And he committed the same sins that his father had committed]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:9. Alternate translation: [when he ruled Israel before him]

3.q: וְ⁠לֹא־הָיָ֨ה לְבָב֤⁠וֹ שָׁלֵם֙ עִם־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י⁠ו כִּ⁠לְבַ֖ב דָּוִ֥ד אָבִֽי⁠ו
3.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:61. Alternate translation: [And he was not completely devoted to Yahweh his God like David his father]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:21. Alternate translation: [his ancestor]

4.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 11:36. Alternate translation: [a successor]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:7. Alternate translation: [by bringing his son to power] or [by allowing his son to rule as king]

The author is speaking of Jerusalem as if it had actually been a building or some other structure that Yahweh could have made **stand**. The author means that Yahweh kept Jerusalem secure. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and by making Jerusalem secure] or [and by protecting Jerusalem]

5.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **right**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what was right]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:10. Alternate translation: [in the judgment of Yahweh]

The author is speaking as if David could actually have **turned** from Yahweh’s commands, as if he had been walking in one direction but then turned to walk in a different direction. The author means that David did not disobey Yahweh’s commands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he had not disobeyed anything that he had commanded him.]

The author is using the term **days** to refer to a specific time, the lifetime of David. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [during his whole lifetime]

6.note: Some ancient manuscripts read “Rehoboam.” The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts read “Abijam.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

7.q: וְ⁠יֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֤י אֲבִיָּם֙ וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה הֲ⁠לֽוֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה
7.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is using phrases that he regularly uses to conclude accounts of kings’ reigns. See how you translated the similar phrases in 11:41–43, 14:19–20, and 14:29–31. Alternate translation: [Now you can read about the rest of the matters of Abijam and all that he did in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah]

8.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:21. Alternate translation: [And Abijam passed away]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:13. Alternate translation: [and people buried him] or [and he was buried]

9.q: וּ⁠בִ⁠שְׁנַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים לְ⁠יָרָבְעָ֖ם מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֥ךְ אָסָ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה
9.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is introducing **Asa** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Judah**. See how you translated the similar phrases in [15:1–2](ta:15).

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **in the year of 20**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [Now in the twentieth year of Jeroboam]

10.note: It is clear from 15:2 that **Maacah** was the mother of Asa’s father, Abijam. Your language may have its own term or expression for this relationship that you can use here and in verse 13. Alternate translation: [his grandmother]

11.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **right**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what was right]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:10. Alternate translation: [in the judgment of Yahweh]

13.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **horror**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a horrid image]

The author is using one person who was involved in this action, **Asa**, to mean everyone who was involved, including Asa’s servants. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Asa ordered his servants to cut down her horror and burn it]

14.note: The author is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [But no one removed the high places] or [But the high places were not removed]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:61. Alternate translation: [Asa was completely devoted to Yahweh]

The author is using the term **days** to refer to a specific time, the lifetime of Asa. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [throughout his lifetime]

15.note: See how you translated the similar expression in [3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]

17.note: See how you translated **went up against** in 14:25. Alternate translation: [And Baasha, the king of Israel, attacked]
See how you translated the similar expression in 12:25. Alternate translation: [and he built up Ramah]

18.q: הַֽ⁠נּוֹתָרִ֣ים ׀ בְּ⁠אוֹצְר֣וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֗ה וְ⁠אֶת־אֽוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית מלך
18.note: The author assumes that his listeners will understand that by the term **remaining**, he means all of the silver and gold articles that were in these storerooms after Shishak had taken the greatest treasures from them, as 14:26 describes. This would include the articles that Asa put in the storerooms after Shishak raided them, as 15:15 describes. Express this meaning in a way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that were then in the storerooms of the house of Yahweh and the storerooms of the house of the king]
See how you translated the similar expression in [7:1](ta:07). Alternate translation: [his royal palace]

The author is using one part these servants, their **hand**, to mean all of them in the act of conveying these silver and gold articles. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he gave them to his servants to convey]

In this verse, the word **hand** is singular in form, but it refers to the hands of all of Asa’s servants. If it would be helpful in your language, if you retain the term “hand,” you could use its plural form. Alternate translation: [the hands of]

The pronoun **them** refers to the silver and gold articles that Asa took from the temple and palace storerooms. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And King Asa sent those articles of silver and gold]

19.q: בְּרִית֙ בֵּינִ֣⁠י וּ⁠בֵינֶ֔⁠ךָ בֵּ֥ין אָבִ֖⁠י וּ⁠בֵ֣ין אָבִ֑י⁠ךָ
19.note: Asa is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Let there be a covenant between me and between you, as there was between my father and between your father]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:14. Alternate translation: [Listen]

Asa is not telling Ben Hadad to **Go** somewhere. He is encouraging him to do what he is suggesting. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. See how you translated the similar expression “come” in 1:12. Alternate translation: [Go ahead and break]
See how you translated the similar expression in 15:17. Alternate translation: [that he may stop attacking me]

20.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 5:8. Alternate translation: [And Ben Hadad agreed to do what King Asa had requested]
See the discussion in the introduction to 1 Kings of this sense of the word “struck.” Alternate translation: [And he attacked]

22.note: In this context, the sense of the word **hear** is that King Asa required all the people of Judah to participate in the work of dismantling Ramah and using its materials to fortify other cities. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And King Asa made all of Judah obey] or [And King Asa required all of Judah to work]

Here, **all of Judah** represents all the men of Judah who were able to work. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And King Asa required the men of Judah to work]

23.q: וְ⁠יֶ֣תֶר כָּל־דִּבְרֵֽי־אָ֠סָא וְ⁠כָל־גְּב֨וּרָת֜⁠וֹ וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה וְ⁠הֶֽ⁠עָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנָ֔ה הֲ⁠לֹֽא־הֵ֣מָּה כְתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה
23.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is using phrases that he regularly uses to conclude accounts of kings’ reigns. See how you translated the similar phrases in 11:41–43 and other comparable contexts in the book. Alternate translation: [Now you can read in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel about the rest of all of the matters of Asa and all of his might and all that he did and the cities that he built]

24.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:21. Alternate translation: [And Asa passed away]

The expression **he was buried** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people buried him]

25.q: וְ⁠נָדָ֣ב בֶּן־יָרָבְעָ֗ם מָלַךְ֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בִּ⁠שְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֔יִם לְ⁠אָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַ⁠יִּמְלֹ֥ךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁנָתָֽיִם
25.note: In this verse, the author is introducing **Nadab** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Israel**. See how you translated the similar phrases in [15:1–2](ta:15) and 15:9–10.
If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **in year two**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [in the second year]

26.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **evil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what was evil]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:10. Alternate translation: [in the judgment of Yahweh]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:3. Alternate translation: [And he lived as his father had lived]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:16. Alternate translation: [and he continued to commit the sin by which he had led the Israelites to sin]

27.q: וַ⁠יִּקְשֹׁ֨ר עָלָ֜י⁠ו בַּעְשָׁ֤א בֶן־אֲחִיָּה֙ לְ⁠בֵ֣ית יִשָּׂשכָ֔ר וַ⁠יַּכֵּ֣⁠הוּ בַעְשָׁ֔א בְּ⁠גִבְּת֖וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַ⁠פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וְ⁠נָדָב֙ וְ⁠כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל צָרִ֖ים עַֽל־גִּבְּתֽוֹן
27.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information that **Nadab and all of Israel were besieging against Gibbethon** before the information that **Baasha … conspired against** Nadab. Alternate translation: [Now Nadab and all of Israel were besieging against Gibbethon, which is to the Philistines. And Baasha, the son of Ahijah, from the house of Issachar, conspired against him, and Baasha struck him at Gibbethon]

The author is introducing **Baasha** as a new participant in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [There was a man named Baasha, the son of Ahijah, from the house of Issachar, and he conspired]

The author is speaking of the tribe of Issachar as if it were actually a **house**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the tribe of Issachar]
See how you translated the similar expression in 11:15. Alternate translation: [and Baasha killed him]

28.note: If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **in year three**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [in the third year]
The pronoun **he** refers to Baasha, and the pronoun **his** refers to Nadab. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Baasha reigned in place of Nadab]

29.note: The author is speaking of all the people descended from Jeroboam as **the house of Jeroboam**. He is envisioning them as if they were one household living together. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Jeroboam]

The word **until** indicates that what follows gives the result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [He did not leave any breathing one to Jeroboam, and as a result, he destroyed him]

The author is using the term **word** to represent what Yahweh said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [according to what Yahweh said when he spoke]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:53. Alternate translation: [through the agency of]

30.q: חַטֹּ֤אות יָרָבְעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֔א וַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
30.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 14:16. Alternate translation: [the sins that Jeroboam committed and caused Israel to commit]

The author is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [by which he severely provoked Yahweh]

31.q: וְ⁠יֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י נָדָ֖ב וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲ⁠לֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
31.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is using phrases that he regularly uses to conclude accounts of kings’ reigns. See how you translated the similar phrases in 11:41–43 and other comparable contexts in the book. Alternate translation: [Now you can read about the rest of the matters of Nadab and all that he did in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel]

32.note: The author is using the term **days** to refer to a specific time, the time when both of these kings were reigning. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the whole time they both reigned]

33.q: בִּ⁠שְׁנַ֣ת שָׁלֹ֔שׁ לְ⁠אָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ בַּעְשָׁ֨א בֶן־אֲחִיָּ֤ה עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּ⁠תִרְצָ֔ה עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְ⁠אַרְבַּ֖ע שָׁנָֽה
33.note: In this verse, the author is reintroducing **Baasha** as a participant in the story, now as the new king of **Israel**. See how you translated the similar phrases in [15:1–2](ta:15) and other comparable contexts in the book.
If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **in year three**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [in the third year]

34.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **evil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what was evil]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:10. Alternate translation: [in the judgment of Yahweh]

34.q: וַ⁠יֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ בְּ⁠דֶ֣רֶךְ יָרָבְעָ֔ם וּ֨⁠בְ⁠חַטָּאת֔⁠וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
34.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 15:26. Alternate translation: [And he lived the way Jeroboam had lived, and he continued to commit the sin by which Jeroboam had led the Israelites to sin]
